Title: Privacy Policy
MetaDescription: How Tedwren collects, uses, shares and protects your personal data, and the rights you have over it.

Sections.Heading: About this policy
Sections.Body: This policy explains how Tedwren Ltd ("Tedwren", "we", "us") collects and uses personal data when you visit this website, enquire about our service, or use the Tedwren platform. It sits alongside our Cookie Policy and Data Protection statement. This is a working draft published for transparency and is subject to legal review before launch.

Sections.Heading: Who we are
Sections.Body: Tedwren Ltd is the data controller for the personal data described here. Our registered office is 5 Rectory Park Close, Sutton Coldfield, B75 7BW, England. You can reach us using the details on our contact page for any question about this policy or your personal data.

Sections.Heading: The personal data we collect
Sections.Body: Account and profile details you give us, such as your name, work email, phone number, employer and role. Workforce and compliance records you add to the platform, which may include qualifications, cards, insurances, inductions, attendance and site-entry decisions. Enquiry details when you contact us, book a demo or apply to the partner programme. Technical and usage data such as IP address, device and browser type, and the pages you view — collected in line with your cookie choices.

Sections.Heading: Where we get it from
Sections.Body: Most personal data comes directly from you or from the organisation that invited you to Tedwren. Some technical data is collected automatically when you use the site. Where an employer or main contractor adds records about a worker, that organisation is responsible for having a lawful basis to share them with us.

Sections.Heading: How we use your data
Sections.Body: To create and administer accounts and provide the platform's features. To keep records current and send expiry and compliance notifications. To respond to enquiries, arrange demos and manage the partner programme. To operate, secure, support and improve the service. To meet legal and regulatory obligations. Where you have agreed, to measure how the website is used so we can improve it.

Sections.Heading: Our lawful bases
Sections.Body: We rely on: performance of a contract, to deliver the service you or your organisation have signed up for; legitimate interests, to run, secure and improve our business in a way that is balanced against your rights; consent, for non-essential analytics cookies and certain marketing, which you can withdraw at any time; and legal obligation, where the law requires us to process data. We do not sell your personal data.

Sections.Heading: Sharing your data
Sections.Body: We share personal data with service providers who process it on our behalf under written terms — for example hosting, email delivery, payment processing and analytics. We may share compliance records with the parties you or your organisation choose to share them with, such as a main contractor viewing a compliance pack. We may disclose data where the law requires it, or to establish, exercise or defend legal claims. We do not allow our providers to use your data for their own purposes.

Sections.Heading: International transfers
Sections.Body: Where personal data is processed outside the UK, we take steps to see that it is protected by an adequacy decision, standard contractual clauses, or another lawful transfer mechanism recognised under UK data-protection law.

Sections.Heading: How long we keep it
Sections.Body: We keep personal data for as long as needed to provide the service and to meet legal, accounting and regulatory requirements. Compliance and evidence records may be retained for longer where they may be needed to demonstrate what happened on a site. When data is no longer needed, we delete it or anonymise it.

Sections.Heading: How we protect it
Sections.Body: We apply technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk — including access controls, encryption in transit, audit logging and supplier due diligence. No online service can promise perfect security, so we also ask you to keep your login credentials confidential. Further detail is on our Security & Trust page.

Sections.Heading: Your rights
Sections.Body: Subject to conditions in law, you can ask to access a copy of your personal data; correct inaccurate data; delete data; restrict or object to certain processing; port data you gave us to another provider; and withdraw consent where we rely on it. To exercise a right, contact us and we will respond within the timeframe set by law. Where the record was added by your employer or a contractor, we may need to direct your request to them as the responsible party.

Sections.Heading: Cookies
Sections.Body: The website uses cookies. No non-essential cookies run before you agree. Full detail — including how to change your choice at any time — is in our Cookie Policy.

Sections.Heading: Children
Sections.Body: The service is intended for use by people in a work context and is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from children.

Sections.Heading: Changes to this policy
Sections.Body: We may update this policy as the service and the law evolve. We will change the review date at the top and, where a change is significant, take reasonable steps to tell you.

Sections.Heading: Contact and complaints
Sections.Body: For any privacy question or to exercise a right, contact us through our contact page. If you are in the UK and are not satisfied with our response, you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) at ico.org.uk.

Title: Cookie Policy
MetaDescription: What cookies Tedwren uses, the categories they fall into, and how you stay in control of them.

Sections.Heading: About this policy
Sections.Body: This policy explains how this website uses cookies and similar technologies, and how you control them. It should be read with our Privacy Policy. This is a working draft published for transparency and is subject to legal review before launch.

Sections.Heading: What cookies are
Sections.Body: Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. Similar technologies such as local storage and pixels work in comparable ways. They let a site remember your actions and preferences and help the site owner understand how the site is used.

Sections.Heading: The categories we use
Sections.Body: Essential cookies make the site work — for example remembering your cookie choice and keeping the site secure. These are always on because the site cannot function properly without them. Analytics cookies, used only with your consent, help us understand which pages are useful so we can improve them.

Sections.Heading: Consent and your control
Sections.Body: When you first visit, we ask for your choice. No analytics or advertising cookies run before you agree. You can reject non-essential cookies in a single click, and both choices are given equal weight. You can change your mind at any time by returning to the cookie controls.

Sections.Heading: First and third-party cookies
Sections.Body: Some cookies are set by Tedwren directly. Analytics may use a third-party provider that sets its own cookies on our behalf under written terms; those providers are not permitted to use the data for their own purposes.

Sections.Heading: Managing cookies in your browser
Sections.Body: You can also control or delete cookies through your browser settings, and set your browser to warn you when a cookie is set. Blocking essential cookies may stop parts of the site from working as intended.

Sections.Heading: Changes to this policy
Sections.Body: As the site changes, the cookies we use may change too. We will update this policy and the review date when that happens.

Sections.Heading: Contact
Sections.Body: For any question about cookies, contact us through our contact page.

Title: Terms of Service
MetaDescription: The terms that govern access to and use of the Tedwren website and platform.

Sections.Heading: About these terms
Sections.Body: These terms govern your access to and use of the Tedwren website and platform provided by Tedwren Ltd, whose registered office is 5 Rectory Park Close, Sutton Coldfield, B75 7BW, England. By using the service you agree to these terms. Where your organisation has signed a separate written agreement with us, that agreement takes precedence if it conflicts with these terms. This is a working draft and is subject to legal review before launch.

Sections.Heading: Eligibility and accounts
Sections.Body: You must be able to form a binding contract to use the service, and use it in a work context. Keep your login credentials secure and the information in your account accurate. You are responsible for activity carried out under your account, and you should tell us promptly if you believe it has been used without your permission.

Sections.Heading: Acceptable use
Sections.Body: Use the service lawfully and only for its intended purpose. Do not attempt to disrupt or gain unauthorised access to the service or its data, upload malicious code, scrape or copy the platform, misuse other people's personal data, or use the service to break the law or infringe others' rights.

Sections.Heading: Your content and data
Sections.Body: You keep ownership of the records and data you put into the platform. You grant us the permissions needed to host and process that data so we can provide the service, as described in our Privacy Policy. You are responsible for having the right to upload the data you add, including workforce records about other people.

Sections.Heading: Compliance evidence
Sections.Body: The platform helps you record and share workforce and compliance information. The records reflect the information entered and the checks performed; you remain responsible for the decisions you take. Tedwren records and shares evidence — it does not take over your legal responsibilities or transfer them to us.

Sections.Heading: Subscriptions, billing and cancellation
Sections.Body: Paid plans are billed as described at sign-up. Worker Passport is an individual annual subscription billed once a year, with a 14-day right to cancel from purchase under UK distance-selling rules; cancelling stops future billing and you keep access for the period already paid for. For organisation plans, charges follow the active usage described on our pricing page. Fees are exclusive of VAT unless stated.

Sections.Heading: Availability and changes
Sections.Body: We work to keep the service available and to improve it over time. We do not promise uninterrupted access, and we may add, change or remove features, or carry out maintenance. Where a change materially reduces the service, we will take reasonable steps to tell affected customers.

Sections.Heading: Third-party services
Sections.Body: The service may link to or rely on third-party services. We are not responsible for third-party services, and your use of them is governed by their own terms.

Sections.Heading: Intellectual property
Sections.Body: The Tedwren platform, website, branding and content are owned by us or our licensors and are protected by law. These terms do not grant you any rights in them beyond the limited right to use the service as intended.

Sections.Heading: Disclaimers
Sections.Body: The service is provided on a reasonable-efforts basis. To the extent permitted by law, we exclude implied warranties. We do not warrant that the service will be error-free or that it will meet every requirement, and you remain responsible for your own compliance obligations.

Sections.Heading: Limitation of liability
Sections.Body: Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law, such as for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud. Subject to that, we are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, or for loss of profit, revenue, goodwill or data, and our total liability is limited to the amount you paid us for the service in the twelve months before the claim.

Sections.Heading: Suspension and termination
Sections.Body: You can stop using the service at any time. We may suspend or end access where these terms are breached, where required by law, or where continued provision would create a security or legal risk. On termination, the rights granted to you end; provisions that by their nature should survive will continue.

Sections.Heading: Governing law
Sections.Body: These terms are governed by the laws of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales have exclusive jurisdiction, unless mandatory local law provides otherwise.

Sections.Heading: Contact
Sections.Body: For any question about these terms, contact us through our contact page.

Title: Data Protection
MetaDescription: How Tedwren meets its data-protection obligations, including controller and processor roles and how to request a DPA.

Sections.Heading: About this statement
Sections.Body: This statement summarises how Tedwren Ltd approaches data protection. It complements our Privacy Policy, which covers how we handle personal data as a controller. This is a working draft published for transparency and is subject to legal review before launch.

Sections.Heading: Our commitment
Sections.Body: We handle personal data in line with UK data-protection law, including the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, and only for the purposes set out in our Privacy Policy. We aim to build data protection into how the platform is designed and operated.

Sections.Heading: Controller and processor roles
Sections.Body: For our own account, enquiry and marketing data, Tedwren is the controller. For workforce and compliance records that a customer organisation manages on the platform, that organisation is generally the controller and Tedwren acts as a processor, handling the data on the customer's documented instructions.

Sections.Heading: Data-processing agreement
Sections.Body: Where we act as a processor, we can provide a data-processing agreement (DPA) setting out the subject matter, duration, nature and purpose of processing, the types of data and categories of data subject, and each party's obligations. Contact us to request one.

Sections.Heading: Sub-processors
Sections.Body: We use vetted sub-processors — for example for hosting, email and payments — under written terms that carry through the data-protection obligations. We keep oversight of our sub-processors and can make information about them available to customers on request.

Sections.Heading: Security measures
Sections.Body: We apply technical and organisational measures appropriate to the risk, such as access controls, encryption in transit, audit logging, backups and supplier due diligence. Further detail is on our Security & Trust page. Security is a shared responsibility: customers should manage their own users and access carefully.

Sections.Heading: International transfers
Sections.Body: Where personal data is transferred outside the UK, we rely on a lawful transfer mechanism such as an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses, together with any additional safeguards that are appropriate.

Sections.Heading: Personal data breaches
Sections.Body: We maintain procedures to detect, investigate and respond to personal data breaches. Where we act as a processor and become aware of a breach affecting a customer's data, we will notify the customer without undue delay and support them in meeting their own obligations.

Sections.Heading: Retention and deletion
Sections.Body: We retain personal data only as long as needed for the purpose it was collected and to meet legal requirements, then delete or anonymise it. Customers can ask us to return or delete their data at the end of a contract, subject to any retention the law requires.

Sections.Heading: Helping you meet data-subject rights
Sections.Body: Where we act as a processor, we assist customers in responding to requests from individuals to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to or port their personal data, so far as the platform allows.

Sections.Heading: Contact
Sections.Body: For data-protection queries, to request a DPA, or to reach the person responsible for data protection, contact us through our contact page.
